review_text: I will start by saying, I do believe that this place fills a niche of customers that just doesn't fit me. I believe that if you are a student needing a place to study, a crack of dawn runner, early morning worker, or small group of workers looking to brainstorm with a little snack, this might be a higher rater place. I have my own place to study and work so the 24-7 hours and condusive study environment are benefits that are lost on me. When looking at the food and drink alone I think this place doesn't hold up. The rice meals dont seem homemade, which is also fine, many restaurants do this, but the price is the same as places that are making homemade rice meals. The meals that look like they are home made are disappointing in my opinion. Coffee taste is just average. The staff are very friendly and helpful, but the place seems a little understaffed when they get busy, so have patience.

Since the Google review page for Martin Asian Cuisine appears to be unavailable, I'm leaving it here under Bloom Cafe, as they share the same space and, I think (?), the same owner, based on the heading of the sales invoice. I had high hopes for Martin Asian Cuisine after reading several positive reviews on other websites, but unfortunately, our experience fell short of expectations. The restaurant is tucked inside Bloom Cafe, which made it a bit tricky to locate at first. We visited on a Sunday lunchtime. The space was small but visually appealing, with natural light streaming in and a thoughtfully designed setup. There were only about five tables, all occupied at the time. Their menu offered a good variety of Asian dishes, which we were excited to try. There was only one waitress serving all customers, and while she was polite and upfront about the expected 30-minute wait time, our food ended up taking over an hour to be served. We only ordered three items: Tom Yum Goong, Goi Cuon, and a chicken dish. One thing to note: only sodas are available for drinks at Martin. If you want something else, you'll have to order separately at Bloom Cafe. We also encountered a minor hygiene issue. One of our bowls had a dead insect stuck to it. While the staff quickly replaced it without question, it did affect our overall impression of the kitchen's attention to cleanliness. As for the food: The Goi Cuon had an overcooked wrapper and oily vegetables, lacking the light and fresh profile we were expecting. The Tom Yum Goong had decent flavor, but it was served lukewarm and the shrimps were overcooked. The chicken dish was okay; similar to inasal with soy sauce. We paid ₱985 for the three dishes. They only accept cash or GCash, which might be inconvenient for some. On the positive side, they were able to provide a sales invoice, which we appreciated. The invoice had Bloom Cafe's name on the header, which further suggests the two businesses are connected. Overall, while the space itself is aesthetically pleasing and has potential, the long waiting time, inconsistent food quality, limited drink service, and minor hygiene concerns made the experience underwhelming. I hope improvements are made in both kitchen operations and customer communication.

They help you to find the right meal and drinks for you. At last the atmosphere. Inside it's cooled and clean. The same goes for the outside. The look is modern. It was undergoing some maintenance when I was there but I still could eat outside. Atmosphere only got 4 instead of 5 stars because it is right beside the main road. So it is very noisy. But apart from that I have nothing to complain. I'd definitely recommend this restaurant. King regards Peter
